could_not_do_FIRST: NO HARDWARE FRAMES YET. Every number below is offline geometry and the shipped `stepCamera` in bare Node. Screenshots/motion at the doorstep are the next step and are NOT claimed.

The 83 counted overlaps are NOT fixed. This piece fixes ONE pair (Thorn writ-house/barge-hold, the pair the ruling names) and freezes the rest behind a ratchet. The other 82 need their own piece; see `the_ruling_verdict` below.

The yaw-blindness in `planSettlement()`'s shrink pass and in `province.js#_deepOverlaps()` is DIAGNOSED, not repaired. Both are shared files with 5 live pieces each; repairing the resolver would re-plan all eight towns and is not a change to make inside someone else's in-flight edit.

`applyInteriorBounds()`'s doorstep derivation is dead code on the shipped world (all 115 interiors take the native RI-WLD13 branch and `continue`), and that branch increments `doorsteps_standable_own_door` 115 times without testing anything. Reported, not fixed — not this piece's file.

the_census.definition: SEPARATION DEPTH (SAT minimum translation distance) between the ORIENTED drawn footprints, the rectangles settlementSolids() actually collides with. depth<=0.36 m (SHELL_WALL_T) = shared wall/terrace, NOT counted. 0.36-1.50 m = borderline (porch/eave/lean-to), reported separately, NOT counted. >1.50 m = counted overlap. `kind:structure` pairs are censused separately and never folded into the headline.
the_census.the_mechanism: 63 of the 83 are INVISIBLE to the shipped check. planSettlement()'s shrink pass and province.js#_deepOverlaps() both compare AXIS-ALIGNED footprints (Dx=|a.x-c.x|, Sx=(aw+cw)/2) while settlementSolids() and buildSettlementExterior() ROTATE the footprint by yaw_deg. 71 of 83 involve at least one yawed building. Thorn's barge hold is declared 7.00 x 16.02 and stands 16.02 x 7.00.
the_census.instrument_proof: node tools/world/building-overlap-census.mjs --self-test — 10 arms, including one that requires the axis-aligned and yawed arms to DISAGREE, and one that requires the yaw-blind AABB view to miss the pair the oriented view catches.

the_falsifier.asked: Are overlaps pervasive AND load-bearing, so separation becomes a layout migration?
the_falsifier.answer: PERVASIVE: yes, decisively — 83 across 8 of 8 settlements, so the ruling's premise of one accidental overlap is dead. LOAD-BEARING: no, not in the way the falsifier feared, and the ruling therefore STANDS for Thorn. 72 of 83 are reachable by the plan's own size-only lever (shrink to the floors), which never moves a position and so cannot break a street layout or a quest coordinate. 11 need a position moved — including 6 pairs authored at a centre gap of 1.0 m or less, and thorn-gate/thorn-house-0 at the IDENTICAL offset_m [-6.86,0,8.6].
the_falsifier.and_the_third_thing_the_ruling_did_not_a: Moving one building is a 7-value edit, not a 2-value edit. All 115 interiors are native RI-WLD13 records, so `door_world_pos`, `apertures[].world_pos`, `exterior_door`, `continuity.exterior_spawn` and `exterior_spawn_declared` are WORLD coordinates in the interior record that do not follow `offset_m`, plus `door` and `door_declared` in the settlement document. That is the door-registration coupling the falsifier named; it is real, it is per-building, and it is why the remaining 82 are a scheduled piece and not a sweep.

the_thorn_fix.chosen: MOVE THE BARGE HOLD, not the writ house. barge-hold offset_m [-20,0,49] -> [-29,0,49]: a pure -9 m translation in x.
the_thorn_fix.why_the_barge_hold: The ruling forbids moving `continuity.exterior_spawn`, and the writ house's is the one it means. Moving the writ house would drag its doorstep with it; moving the barge hold leaves the writ house, its door and its doorstep byte-for-byte unchanged.
the_thorn_fix.why_-9x_and_not_further: Measured, not argued. Six candidate offsets were scored on a control clone with the shipped `stepCamera` (72 bearings). -9x is the smallest move that reaches the best score any candidate reaches, and it leaves a 1.99 m alley between the two buildings rather than shoving a quay building off its quay.
the_thorn_fix.why_a_pure_translation: Every relative geometry of the barge hold — its door on its own wall, its doorstep in front of that door, its aperture — is preserved exactly. Only its relation to the writ house changes.
